summary: Remote-controlled PTY/SSH daemon with self-replacing upgrade channel
details: The package's main/bin entrypoint runs a daemon that opens a WebSocket connection to a vendor-controlled server and drives a local PTY (via optional node-pty) and SSH2 sessions on the installer's host, executing commands received over that channel. Bundle strings include WebSocketProxyAgent, ptyProcess handling, daemonMcpServer, and loopback tunnels to 127.0.0.1:3389 (RDP), 127.0.0.1:5900/5901 (VNC), giving the remote peer interactive shell and desktop/tunnel access to the machine. In addition, an upgradeWhalentAgent / upgrade.js module accepts and installs replacement builds of @whalent/agent-core delivered by the same vendor server at runtime, outside npm's update flow — the README itself states the package is 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades.' The entire 14 MB dist/index.cjs is obfuscator.io-encoded with a rotated 109,659-entry string array, numeric-checksum self-integrity loop, and _0xXXXX identifiers applied even to vendored OSS, which prevents audit of the exact command surface exposed to the remote peer and of what the upgrader will accept and execute. Whoever controls the Whalent server (legitimately or through compromise of that server) has arbitrary code execution on every host running this agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
